scope: Theorem 1.2 (Deficit at a prescribed price) of the manuscript “Generalized ionization energies for full Coulomb atoms” (preprints/Generalized-ionization-energies-for-full-Coulomb-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 263 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1450c11be0743629), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal number q > 0 such that, for every sequence satisfying λ = s−4 , s −→ 0, Zs3 −→ ∞, and every choice of n minimizing En + λn, one has s3 (Z − n) −→ q. The number q is the exterior Coulomb charge of the unique classical solution, tending uniformly to zero at infinity, of ∆F = 4πk ( (F − 1)+ )3/2 on R3 \ {0}, k = (5T/3)−3/2 , that is bounded above and below by positive multiples of |x|−4 near zero. The density k((F −1)+)3/2 has bounded support, and F(x) = q/|x| outside that support. Moreover, aTF = 3 7 q−4/3 .
